headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from ChatGPT Desktop’s file/screen/clipboard ingestion paired with a separate RL agent; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read files, clipboard, screenshots, and supported-app content by default, so malicious content could be ingested if B’s outputs are copied into those surfaces. Agent B exposes no ingestion surface, so the pairwise pathway is indirect and not documented, but A’s trusted parsing of external content makes injection plausible.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs are copied into agent_a clipboard or uploaded files
IF agent_a is asked to interpret content from supported macOS apps or screenshots
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for this workflow
Use a plain-text intermediary and strip instructions before paste
Review any copied B output in a separate viewer first
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content
requires-engineering: isolate A from untrusted file/screen inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while B has no documented data classes or egress. The pair can still leak sensitive material if A’s captured context is forwarded into B’s simulation inputs or logs; the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests sensitive uploads or screenshots
IF those contents are then exported into agent_b inputs, logs, or training artifacts
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in A’s workspace
Redact files before any handoff to B
Turn off unnecessary screen capture and clipboard use
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
requires-engineering: add retention controls for transferred artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, and B has no documented write or network capabilities. That makes direct resource contention unlikely; the only plausible conflict is user-mediated workflow interference, which is small and non-default.
conditions: IF the operator manually routes both agents to the same mutable external resource
IF B is embedded in a workflow that writes shared state outside its documented profile
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use read-only exports between agents
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce screen/file-derived outputs, but B is a game-playing RL agent with no documented action-taking authority or input-acceptance pipeline. Without evidence that B treats A’s output as authoritative, the cascade is limited to manual workflow mistakes rather than an automated harmful chain.
conditions: IF the operator feeds A-generated text directly into B as authoritative state
IF B is configured to act on external instructions rather than simulation inputs
mitigations: Verify A outputs before reuse
Keep A as a drafting tool only
Do not automate A-to-B handoff
requires-engineering: add validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A is a closed-source OpenAI desktop product that handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code; B is open-source and appears local/simulation-only with no data classes or egress. The main compliance issue is mismatch in handling sensitive data classes, but B’s profile does not show a residency or certification conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a uploads, screenshots, or connected IDEs
IF the operator requires a documented residency or retention policy for the combined workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs
Review vendor retention terms before use
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
